patent: Filed 1947-11-13 and issued 1953-03-17 to Frank Gray of Bell Telephone Laboratories. It introduces the "reflected binary code", in which the code groups for neighbouring values differ in exactly one digit; the code is now generally called the Gray code after this patent. The problem it addresses is the electron-beam coding tube used for pulse code modulation at Bell Labs (described by R. W. Sears in the Bell System Technical Journal, vol. 27, January 1948): with a conventional binary mask, a beam that strays to an adjacent row can emit a code far from either value (seven, 0111, next to eight, 1000), while with a reflected mask the error is at most one level (FIGS. 2, 2A). The patent also gives the conversion rules between the two codes (Formulae 1 and 2), a direct weighted evaluation of a reflected code group (Formulae 4), and three receivers built on them (FIGS. 3-5). The ordering itself was older (it is the solution sequence of the Chinese rings puzzle, analysed by Louis Gros in 1872); this patent named it and applied it to analog-to-digital coding. Gray codes are now standard in shaft and position encoders, in the cell order of Karnaugh maps, in the bit labelling of digital modulation constellations, and in counters passed between clock domains.

figs.1: Transmitter coder. Voice source 23 (drawn as a microphone) is sampled by 24; the sample held on condenser 28 sets, through amplifier 30 and plates 12, the vertical position of beam 11, i.e. which row of mask 15 it will cross. Sawtooth generator 33 and sweep amplifier 34 then drive plates 13 to sweep the beam along that row; current passing the apertures reaches collector 14 and appears across resistor 27 as the code group, which is regenerated (37), inverted (39) and sent on line 40. Pulse generator 26 times multivibrators 25 and 32 and, over conductor 38, the regenerator; switch 36 picks electrode 18 or 19 for blanking the return sweep.
figs.2: The 7-digit reflected binary mask, one column per digit, D7 (most significant) at left so that the sweep crosses it first. Each of the 128 rows is one level, values increasing upward: the single D7 aperture covers the upper half. Every column except D7 is mirror-symmetric about the horizontal center line, and each aperture is centered on an end of an aperture in the column to its left. The arrowed dash line marks level thirty-eight: it crosses apertures in D6, D5, D3 and D1, i.e. 0110101.
figs.2A: The prior-art conventional binary mask at the same scale. Aperture counts double from column to column (1 in D7 to 64 in D1), so its D1 apertures are half the height of those in FIG. 2 (32 in D1 there). At many row boundaries several columns change at once; at mid-height, rows 63 (0111111) and 64 (1000000) differ in every column. The same thirty-eight line crosses D6, D3 and D2: 0100110.
figs.3: Receiver that first converts to conventional binary. Incoming pulses (A), regenerated by 42, go through condensers 43, 44 to two flip-flops (45, 46 above; 45', 46' below) used on alternate groups. Each pulse toggles the flip-flop, so its output (B) after each digit is the modulo-2 sum of the reflected digits received so far, which by Formulae 1 is the conventional digit. Distributor 53, stepped by the timing chain 54-59 recovered from the pulse train, applies battery 52 to reset and hold one flip-flop while the other translates; phase shifter 61 sets the framing. Regenerators 62, 62' re-time the outputs (C), and decoders 65, 65' feed reproducer 64 through distributor 66, which the dash-dot line ties to 53.
figs.4: Alternative to FIG. 3 with a counting tube in place of each flip-flop, in two like channels (primed numerals: lower channel, which counts in negative steps). Each incoming pulse (A), through amplifier 72 and diode 71, adds a fixed charge to condenser 70, so its voltage rises in equal steps (B). That voltage moves beam 77 of tube 74 along mask 78, whose slots are separated by bars of equal height; each step moves the beam from bar to slot or slot to bar, so the collector output (C) changes level at every pulse, as the flip-flop output does. Triodes 81, 81', switched by distributor 53, discharge and hold one condenser while the other channel counts; one regenerator 85 and decoder 87 serve both channels. Waveform D at the regenerator output is not discussed in the text.
figs.5: Direct decoder: no code conversion and a single flip-flop 90, 91 that is never reset. Its output (B) is differentiated by 92, 93 into spikes (C) and squared by 94 into pulses (D) that repeat the incoming code with alternate pulses inverted. These feed six delay devices 95a-95f in parallel (95a longest, delays differing by one pulse period) plus an undelayed path, so all seven digits of a group arrive together at conductances 96a-96g, marked 1.27 down to .01 micromho, i.e. weights 127, 63, 31, 15, 7, 3, 1. Feedback amplifier 97 adds them, sampler 99 takes the sum once per group, and rectifier 100 discards its sign, which depends only on the polarity of the first pulse. This is Formulae 4 in hardware.

glossary.def: Sampling a signal, quantizing each sample to one of a fixed set of levels, and sending the level number as a group of on-or-off pulses.

Binary code in which the groups for successive numbers differ in one digit only; now called Gray code. Built by writing a list, then its mirror image below it, and prefixing 0 to the first half and 1 to the second.
Ordinary positional binary numbers, digit d weighted 2^(d-1).
The pulses (seven here) that represent one sample.
Perforated plate in a cathode ray coding tube; the row the beam is swept along sets which pulse positions are filled.
Arithmetic modulo two: even sums are 0, odd sums 1 (exclusive OR).
Two-tube circuit with two stable states that changes state on each input pulse.
Diode-condenser charge pump that adds an equal step of voltage to a storage condenser for each input pulse, so its voltage counts pulses.
Circuit that cuts a pulse train at a threshold and gates it at the pulse clock to restore clean, correctly timed pulses.
Monostable multivibrator: one output pulse of set length per trigger.
Multivibrator used as a frequency divider (7 to 1 here).
Rotating switch that connects a source to several circuits in turn; here it alternates the two translating channels.
Aligning the receiver to the start of each code group.
Unit of conductance, now the siemens; micromho = microsiemens.
Vacuum tubes with three or five electrodes; a saturated pentode passes a nearly constant current.
